draft.title: Left carotid endarterectomy with endovascular patch angioplasty - fictional cardiology report

sections.heading: Clinical history
sections.body: The patient has chronic renal failure and known critical carotid artery stenosis. The patient was admitted to hospital the previous day with chest pain and has been considered for coronary artery bypass grafting. Bilateral carotid endarterectomy was planned, but cardiac catheterization was felt to be necessary first. The left carotid stenosis was more severe and was addressed first.

sections.heading: Preoperative and postoperative diagnosis
sections.body: Preoperative diagnosis: critical left carotid stenosis. Postoperative diagnosis: critical left carotid stenosis.

sections.heading: Procedure and anaesthesia
sections.body: Procedure performed: left carotid endarterectomy with endovascular patch angioplasty. Anaesthesia: cervical block.

sections.heading: Intraoperative findings
sections.body: An atherosclerotic plaque was seen in the common carotid artery extending into the internal carotid artery. The internal carotid artery was quite tortuous. The external carotid artery was occluded at its origin. After endarterectomy, the external carotid artery back-bled well and the internal carotid artery had good backflow bleeding.

sections.heading: Technique
sections.body: The patient was positioned supine and the neck, shoulder and chest wall were prepared and draped. A longitudinal incision was made along the anterior border of the left sternocleidomastoid muscle. The common carotid, internal carotid beyond the plaque, external carotid and superior thyroid arteries were isolated and encircled with tape. Facial veins were ligated and divided. The ansa cervicalis, hypoglossal and vagus nerves were identified and preserved. The patient received 5000 units of heparin before vessel control. Vessels were controlled with clips and clamps and a longitudinal arteriotomy was made along the common carotid artery and extended onto the internal carotid artery. Endarterectomy was performed and the vessel was flushed with heparinised saline. The internal carotid artery was shortened by imbrication with horizontal mattress sutures. An endovascular patch was cut to size and sutured in place with continuous suture, and the vessels were flushed before the clamps were released in sequence. The patient remained neurologically intact throughout. The patient received an additional 7000 units of heparin during the endarterectomy.

sections.heading: Closure
sections.body: The wound was irrigated with antibiotic solution. Counts were correct and haemostasis was good. The incision was closed in layers with absorbable suture and staples.

draft.impression: Left carotid endarterectomy with endovascular patch angioplasty was performed for critical left carotid stenosis in a patient with chronic renal failure. The patient remained neurologically intact during the procedure. Intraoperative flow was good in both the external and internal carotid arteries after repair.

draft.title: Discharge summary: syncope, end-stage renal disease and congestive heart failure

sections.body: The patient was given fluids and orthostatic checks were negative. Because fluid had been given beforehand, orthostatic hypotension could not be ruled out.

sections.body: The patient was admitted with likely orthostatic hypotension and was found to be hypotensive on admission. Coreg was held for hypotension and later restarted at 6.25 mg twice daily, which was well tolerated. Cardiology reduced lisinopril to 5 mg daily and ordered a nuclear medicine myocardial perfusion stress test. Nephrology performed dialysis the day after admission and Renal considered the presyncopal symptoms likely due to decreased intravascular volume after dialysis. Renal agreed with the lisinopril reduction and the Coreg dose reduction, and advised that Procrit should continue. On the day the stress test was scheduled, the patient was reluctant to proceed because of fear of needles and concern about risks. The risks were explained as quite low, but the patient chose to discharge self against medical advice.

draft.impression: The patient was admitted with syncope, most likely from low blood pressure after dialysis or on standing, in the setting of end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, congestive heart failure and hypertension. Hemostasis was achieved with 10 minutes of pressure. The patient was transferred to the intensive care unit, where extubation was performed without any deficits.

Right internal carotid injection: the right internal carotid artery was of normal calibre, with opacification of the right ophthalmic and posterior communicating arteries. The right A1 supplied both A2 segments, with no spasm of the distal anterior cerebral artery. The right MCA and its distal branches filled normally, with normal capillary filling and venous drainage. Post-papaverine images: the internal carotid artery and anterior cerebral artery showed increased calibre. The previously clipped left ICA bifurcation aneurysm was well clipped, with no residual neck and no filling of the aneurysm dome.

draft.title: Coronary Angiography and Left Heart Catheterization Report

sections.heading: Clinical history
sections.body: The patient presented with a non-ST elevation myocardial infarction. Risks, benefits and alternatives were explained, and informed consent was obtained verbally and in writing.

sections.heading: Procedures performed
sections.body: Left heart catheterization and bilateral selective coronary angiography. A left ventriculogram was not performed.

sections.heading: Technique
sections.body: The right femoral region was prepared and draped sterilely and the skin was infiltrated with 1% lidocaine. The right femoral artery was cannulated with an #18 gauge needle and a guidewire, and a sheath was placed. A Judkins left #4 catheter was used to engage the left main coronary artery and the left coronary system was imaged in several views using hand injections of nonionic contrast. A Judkins right #4 catheter was then used to engage the right coronary artery and the right coronary system was imaged in several views using hand injections of nonionic contrast. The left ventricular end-diastolic pressure was measured during catheter rotation. The sheath was flushed at the end of the procedure.

sections.heading: Findings
sections.body: Left main coronary artery: moderate calibre, bifurcating into the left anterior descending and circumflex arteries, with no haemodynamically significant stenosis. Left anterior descending artery: moderate calibre, subtotally occluded in the mid portion over about 1 to 1.5 cm with TIMI-I flow distally; the distal portion is diffusely diseased and the proximal portion has minor irregularities; the first diagonal branch has minor irregularities throughout. Circumflex artery: moderate calibre, with a 60% proximal lesion and a 90% mid lesion before the first obtuse marginal branch, which has minor irregularities throughout. Right coronary artery: moderate calibre and dominant, with a 90% mid stenotic lesion; it gives off the posterior descending and posterolateral arteries. Left ventricular end-diastolic pressure was approximately 22 mmHg. ST elevation in the inferior leads occurred during contrast injection and resolved after the injection finished.

sections.heading: Plan
sections.body: The patient will be transferred to another hospital today for likely percutaneous coronary intervention of the mid left anterior descending lesion, with surgical evaluation for coronary artery bypass grafting. The findings and plan were discussed with the patient.

The patient is planned for transfer for likely intervention and surgical evaluation.

draft.title: Cerebral Imaging and Neurological Assessment Report

sections.heading: Clinical history
sections.body: The patient has a history of two strokes, one in 11/90 and one in 11/91. The patient was stable until 12/31/92, when confusion developed with left-sided weakness and difficulty speaking. These symptoms resolved within hours and recurred the following day. Local evaluation with head CT (HCT) showed an old right parietal stroke. Carotid duplex scan reported a 'high grade stenosis' of the right internal carotid artery (RICA). The patient was transferred to UIHC Vascular Surgery for carotid endarterectomy, but the confusion persisted, and the patient was seen by Neurology on 1/8/93 and transferred to Neurology on 1/11/93.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body: Past history includes cholecystectomy, bilateral inguinal herniorrhaphies, alcohol use of 3-10 beers per day, a right parietal stroke in 10/87 with residual left hemiparesis (leg worse than arm), and a second stroke in the distant past of unspecified type. No medicines on admission. Family history includes Alzheimer's disease and stroke on the paternal side. The patient has a smoking history of more than 50 pack-years. Review of systems showed no weight loss, with poor appetite and selective eating.

sections.heading: Examination
sections.body: Blood pressure 137/70, heart rate 81, respiratory rate 13, oxygen saturation 95%, afebrile. Mental state: oriented to city and month but not to date or hospital; naming and verbal comprehension intact; could indicate the direction of Iowa City and Des Moines from Clinton and recalled 2-3 objects after two minutes, both only with assistance; misspelled 'world' backwards as 'dlow'. Cranial nerves unremarkable apart from neglect of the left visual field to double simultaneous stimulation. Motor: reduced power in the left arm and leg, most marked at the deltoid, biceps and hip flexors. Sensation intact to pinprick, light touch and vibration. Coordination: dysdiadochokinesis on the right and left. Dyssynergic right upper limb on finger-to-nose testing. Reflexes 2+ throughout the upper limbs and at the patellae, absent at the ankles. Right plantar response flexor; left plantar equivocal.

sections.heading: Investigations
sections.body: Full blood count normal apart from a raised mean corpuscular volume of 103 fL (normal 82-98). Urinalysis showed more than 20 white cells; the patient was treated for a urinary tract infection with amoxicillin. Glucose, TSH, free T4, VDRL, ANA and RF were unremarkable. Vitamin B12 was reduced at 139 pg/mL (normal 232-1137). Schilling test was inconclusive because a 24-hour urine collection could not be completed. Empiric vitamin B12 1000 mcg intramuscularly daily for 7 days, then monthly, along with thiamine 100 mg daily, folate 1 mg daily and aspirin 325 mg daily. ESR and CRP were elevated on admission and fell as the infection was treated. EEG showed diffuse slowing with focal theta-delta slowing over the right temporal area.

sections.heading: Imaging findings
sections.body: Head CT with contrast on 1/19/93 showed a gyriform enhancing lesion in the left parietal lobe consistent with a new infarct, and an old hypodense area in the right parietal lobe consistent with an old infarct. Cerebral angiogram showed 90% stenosis of the RICA and 50% stenosis of the left internal carotid artery (LICA).

sections.heading: Follow-up
sections.body: The confusion was attributed to the urinary tract infection in the setting of old and new strokes and vitamin B12 deficiency. The patient was lost to follow-up and did not undergo carotid endarterectomy.

draft.impression: Head CT showed a new left parietal infarct and an old right parietal infarct. Cerebral angiography showed 90% right and 50% left internal carotid artery stenosis. EEG showed diffuse slowing with focal theta-delta slowing over the right temporal area. The patient was lost to follow-up and did not undergo the planned carotid endarterectomy.

draft.title: Bilateral Carotid Cerebral and Right Femoral-Popliteal Angiogram Report

sections.heading: Preoperative diagnoses
sections.body: 1. Carotid artery occlusive disease. 2. Peripheral vascular disease.

sections.heading: Postoperative diagnoses
sections.body: 1. Carotid artery occlusive disease. 2. Peripheral vascular disease.

sections.heading: Procedures performed
sections.body: 1. Bilateral carotid cerebral angiogram. 2. Right femoral-popliteal angiogram.

sections.heading: Findings
sections.body: Right carotid cerebral system: the right internal carotid artery was very tortuous with kinking in its cervical portions, but no focal stenosis was noted. The intracranial portion of the right internal carotid artery and the right middle cerebral artery showed no significant disease. Left carotid cerebral system: the cervical portion of the left internal carotid artery showed a 30 to 40% stenosis with a small ulcer crater present. The intracranial portion of the left internal carotid artery and the left middle cerebral artery showed no significant disease. Right lower extremity: no significant disease was seen.

sections.heading: Procedure
sections.body: With the patient in supine position under local anesthesia plus intravenous sedation, the groin areas were prepped and draped in a sterile fashion. The common femoral artery was punctured in a retrograde fashion and a 5-French introducer sheath was advanced under fluoroscopic guidance. A catheter was placed in the aortic arch and the right and left common carotid arteries were selectively catheterized and visualized. Heparin had been given initially and was reversed with protamine. The catheter and introducer sheath were removed, firm pressure was held over the puncture site for 20 minutes, and a sterile Coverlet dressing and sandbag compression were applied. The patient tolerated the procedure well throughout.

The right internal carotid artery is very tortuous with kinking in its cervical portions but has no focal stenosis.
